messages:
Maya: Heads-up — we started seeing client failures from eu-west that only show up when requests go over IPv6. IPv4 traffic looks normal. Couple of customer reports + our synthetic checks. Anyone else?

Liam: saw this too. 
- spike in 5xx around 08:12 UTC
- logs show connections from ::ffff:64:... (NAT64) timing out to our backend pool
- tcpdump from node shows a few SYNs but no server response

Anita: Important detail: the LBs were configured for dualstack but the VPC in that region never got an IPv6 CIDR assigned, so the NLB/ALB never actually got IPv6 ENIs. In other words DNS AAAA records are missing or pointing to NAT64 proxies we don't control.

Maya: That explains why mobile clients on IPv6-only networks hit a translator and then fail. Some clients (iOS/Android on carrier IPv6 NAT64) try IPv6 first and don't fall back cleanly.

Liam: Repro steps I used:
```
# shows no AAAA for service domain
dig +short AAAA api.eu-west.redwood.example.com
# test direct IPv6 connect (fails)
curl -6 -v https://api.eu-west.redwood.example.com --resolve "api.eu-west.redwood.example.com:443:2500:dead:beef::1"
# ipv4 still works
curl -4 -v https://api.eu-west.redwood.example.com
```

Anita: On k8s side the service manifest currently has: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: edge-nlb
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: nlb
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
    - port: 443
  selector: { app: edge }
```
We need to add ipFamilyPolicy + the aws dualstack annotation or allocate IPv6 to the subnet. Example we should try in staging: 
```
metadata:
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ip-address-type: "dualstack"
spec:
  ipFamilyPolicy: PreferDualStack
  ipFamilies:
    - IPv4
    - IPv6
```
Note: AWS requires VPC IPv6 CIDR/subnet IPv6 and NLB support in region.

net-bot: Synthetic check failed: eu-west ping over IPv6 (NAT64) — TLS handshake timeout — 1710723480 UTC.

Maya: Two problems to coordinate: (1) DNS — we currently do not publish AAAA for this host in eu-west; (2) infra — if we enable dualstack on k8s Service but VPC lacks IPv6, LB won't bind. We also have clients behind NAT64 that will attempt IPv6 and hit some cloud NAT64 which rewrites the A-to-AAAA resolution.

Liam: Quick mitigation options: 
- Short-term: publish IPv6 AAAA that points to our Cloudflare proxy (CF can proxy dualstack even if origin is IPv4). That buys clients a working path without changing VPC.
- Medium: allocate IPv6 CIDR to VPC + update subnets + recreate/annotate LB services in a maintenance window.
- Fallback: region-specific DNS rule to serve A only (no AAAA) so IPv6-only clients get NX and may fallback to IPv4 — but that's not reliable for NAT64-only networks.

Anita: Caveats: 
- NAT64 behavior: if DNS returns AAAA synthesized by carrier (for A-only origin), some clients will connect to NAT64 and we see ::ffff:... sources which mess up IP allowlists and geo checks.
- TLS SNI is fine generally, but some middleboxes rewrite SNI or drop ALPN; we've seen handshakes fail when proxies translate endpoints.

SRE Oncall: created incident INC-2026-1293 and assigned to eng-infra, linking this thread. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-1293

Maya: Proposed immediate action plan:
1) Add IPv6 AAAA via Cloudflare (proxy mode) for eu-west to restore client connectivity — roll to 10% with DNS weight.
2) Enable synthetic IPv6-only checks in EU and US edge to detect regressions.
3) Schedule infra work to allocate IPv6 CIDR to VPC and test dualstack NLB in staging next week.
4) Update runbooks for IP allowlists to accept ::ffff:0:0/96 mapping if we keep NAT64 in front.

Liam: I'll put together the k8s svc patch and a terraform change for Cloudflare entry. Will test in staging and post results here.

Anita: I'll coordinate with cloud infra to reserve IPv6 on the VPC and confirm subnet support; also check quota for elastic IPv6 addresses if needed.

ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance window request submitted for 2026-03-20 02:00-04:00 UTC — pending approvals.

Maya: TL;DR: dualstack name is enabled but VPC lacked IPv6, causing missing AAAA and clients hitting NAT64 -> timeouts. Short-term CF proxy AAAA, medium-term enable VPC IPv6 + dualstack LB, long-term add IPv6 synthetic coverage and docs.

Liam: :thumbsup:
Anita: :eyes:
SRE Oncall: I'll update the incident with the runbook steps and keep watch on synthetic alerts.

Maya: Thanks — will follow up with postmortem if this spikes again.
